title: Go-to-Scale Readout and Operational Scan
body:
Purpose: quick, operational-first readout to decide whether this feature (beta -> tiered public) can enter staged scale. This doc is a compact scan: KPI snapshot, capacity runway, phased rollout gates, and immediate actions for the next 14 days.

Scope: product features hitting inference runtime and routing logic (hosted API + dedicated fallback). Focus areas: latency SLOs, per-token cost trajectory, dedicated capacity commitments, and rollback/fallback controls. Not a product spec — this is an operational checkpoint to inform go/no-go and staffing.

Executive snapshot (one-pager):
- Decision window: 2025-02-07 go/no-go for phased public ramp (tiered traffic 0.5%->5%->25% over 3 weeks).
- Primary owner: Priya Malhotra (product-ops). Oncall lead: Marcus Reid (SRE).
- Baseline KPIs (current beta->canary):
  - 95th pct latency (gen): 170ms (target <= 200ms)
  - Error rate (5m rolling): 0.8% (target <= 1.0%)
  - Cost per 1M tokens (hosted): $28 (target <= $30)
  - KV cache hit rate (prefix): 22% (target >= 30% across 48h workload)
  - Request concurrency headroom: 18% (operational threshold >= 15%)
  - Model fallback incidence: 3 calls/day (expected 0 for stable)

Capacity runway and assumptions:
- Committed Dedicated GPUs: 12xA10g-equivalent (baseline). Can scale +6 within 24h via burst pool but billed at premium.
- Expected peak token throughput at 5% = 2.1B tokens/day (est). Needs 18 GPU-hours above baseline to sustain 95th pct targets.
- Cost sensitivity: 10% traffic increase -> ~8% token cost increase if caching unchanged. If KV cache bump to 40% -> 5% cost reduction at 25% traffic.
- Open capacity risks:
  - Burst quota negotiated but needs legal signoff for overage (Contact: Sofia Alvarez).
  - Region-specific GPU availability (APAC) may add cross-region latency; downgrade policy required.

Phased rollout plan (operational gates):
- Phase 0: Internal canary (done). Observability: latency traces, token-level cost, end-to-end errors instrumented.
- Phase 1: Tiered public (0.5% traffic for 24h). Gate: no >1.5x baseline error spikes, no sustained 95th pct >250ms.
- Phase 2: Ramp to 5% (72h soak). Gate: SLOs stable, cost delta acceptable, KV cache >=30% or plan to mitigate.
- Phase 3: 25% (7 days staggered). Gate: automated rollback pass/fail tests and dedicated capacity hold.
- Phase 4: Full rollout (post review).

Preflight checklist (quick hits) — must be green before Phase 1:
- [ ] Canary observability dashboard (latency, errors, fallback count) reviewed and bookmarked by all owners. (owner: Daniel Kim)
- [ ] Canary synthetic probe suite run (1000 prods/min) — baseline artifacts attached. (owner: Marcus Reid)
- [ ] Billing alert: projected daily spend > threshold triggers Slack #finance-alert. (owner: Sofia Alvarez)
- [ ] Fallback policy verified: model variant mapping + per-region routing fallback tested end-to-end. (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Runbook for rollback created and staged in #ops-runbooks with clear steps and comms templates. (owner: Marcus)
- [ ] Customer-facing comms draft for beta customers and newsletters (PRD link). (owner: Product Marketing)

Canary triggers / automated abort conditions (these must auto-stop ramp and page oncall):
- sustained error rate > 2% for 10m
- 95th pct latency > 300ms for > 5m
- cost burn > 2x expected for 1h without cache change
- KV cache hit rate drops > 10 percentage points vs baseline for 15m

Operational playbook snippets:
- Fast rollback: switch route -> compatible smaller model variant in same region, disable feature flags, throttle traffic to 10rps/customer. Estimated user impact: degraded quality but preserved availability.
- Degrade gracefully: enable CPU-only fallback path for read-only features (embeddings) until GPU pool recovers.
- Surge management: pause non-essential background batches, drop prefetch tasks.

KPI measurement plan (what we'll track during each phase):
- Primary: 95th pct latency, 99th pct tail, 5m error rate, token/sec throughput, cache hit %, per-1M token cost (rolling 24h).
- Secondary: feature-level adoption, per-customer latency percentile, rerank/degenerate response rate (quality signal).
- Reporting cadence: automated deck to execs at 09:00 PST daily during Phase 2+; sync for ops + SRE at 11:00 PST.

Ownership + escalation contacts:
- Product-ops (overall): Priya Malhotra (pri@redwood.com)
- SRE / Oncall lead: Marcus Reid (marcus@redwood.com)
- Observability + Dashboards: Daniel Kim (daniel@redwood.com)
- Finance / Cost alerts: Sofia Alvarez (sofia@redwood.com)
- Legal (overage/contract): Laura Chen (laura@redwood.com)
- Exec stake: VP Product: Amina Torres (amina@redwood.com)

Open questions / unknowns (notes to self):
- What is the explicit overage rate for burst GPUs? need contract caveat (Sofia to confirm).
- Can dedicated capacity be preempted by higher SLAs? Confirm with infra (ticket SRE-210).
- How stable is the model variant mapping under seq len=2048 tests? observed mild cache thrash.
- Need an SLO for quality (func correctness) — define measurable eval set or revert heuristics.

Immediate next actions (next 48h):
1) Daniel: finalize canary deck + add cost-per-minute chart. (ETA: 2025-01-17)
2) Marcus: run extended synthetic soak 24h with traffic shape for 5% and attach traces. (ETA: 2025-01-18)
3) Sofia: confirm burst pricing & legal overage clause. (ETA: 2025-01-19)
4) Priya: finalize rollback comms and schedule go/no-go meeting 2025-02-06. (ETA: 2025-01-20)

Appendix (quick links & artifacts):
- Confluence: /product/ops/scale-readout-2025 (designs, history)
- JIRA: PRODOPS-243 (rollout orchestration), SRE-189 (canary failures)
- GitHub: PR 812 (traffic router changes)
- Synthetic deck: attached asset id in GDrive (see linked artifacts)

Notes / rough:
- Quick conservative heuristic: keep cost budget headroom 20% for first 2 weeks of ramp. If cost burn < 10% of projection -> green.
- Consider temporary promo credits for early customers to offset higher cost while cache warms.
- This doc intentionally terse — capture decisions in meeting notes; move to final playbook if go-ahead.

End of readout.
